newsitem.title: UK: Sinn Fein's Adams denied U.S. visa -newspaper.
newsitem.headline: Sinn Fein's Adams denied U.S. visa -newspaper.

text.p: The United States has denied Sinn Fein president Gerry Adams a visitor's visa in a new clampdown against the organisation, the Sunday Times newspaper reported.
It said Adams was told of the decision last month and that he had said last week he had changed his plans to visit the United States.
But Sinn Fein spokesman Richard McAuley denied Adams had even applied for a visa.
He said Adams had considered going there next month to promote his autobiography "Before the Dawn" but decided not to travel anywhere before Britain's national election, due by May.
"There are no plans for Gerry to travel anywhere until the election is out of the way," he said.
A spokesman at the U.S. embassy in london said he had no knowledge of Adams applying for a visa.
Adams has visited the U.S. five times since he was first, and controversially, given a visa in February 1994. The decision enraged the British government.

In December Adams challenged a decision by the Australian government to deny him a visa. Australian authorities said they had turned him down on the grounds that he was not a person of good character because of Sinn Fein's links with the Irish Republican Army (IRA).
Sinn Fein is banned from talks on the future of Northern Ireland because the IRA refuses to reinstate a ceasefire broken a year ago.
Police, politicians and residents of the province all fear Northern Ireland could quickly return to all-out guerrilla warfare over British rule.
